analysis.title: Core inflation starts biting
key_insights: US October core CPI was strong in quantity (0.3% MoM SA for the third month in a row) and in quality: OER (rent), car insurance and recreation services were all strong, and volatile components cannot be blamed this time.

Airfares, a volatile component, were a downside surprise versus CA-CIB's estimate. Core goods came in weaker than expected overall, but core goods excluding the volatile component were stronger than expected.
The 1Y TIPS breakeven widened by around 10bp after the CPI release.
The strong CPI plus last Friday's hot employment report should essentially lock in a Fed hike at the December meeting. CA-CIB's base case is a 25bp hike.

Earlier US core CPI prints of about 0.3% MoM in August and September were largely driven by noisy components (airlines, hotels, telephone services), so they carried a weak signal. June's -0.02% MoM SA core CPI was a noise print on the other side.
Eurozone preliminary October core HICP was 2.54% YoY, 8bp above CA-CIB's 2.46% preview. Part of the strength came from noisy components (hotels, clothing), but not all of it.
CA-CIB expects Eurozone core inflation to accelerate to 2.6% at year-end and 2.8-2.9% in early 2027, even though energy prices have eased recently.
Higher natural gas and oil prices and a lower EUR/USD point to an upward revision of the ECB's core HICP forecasts. Tighter financial conditions are the only significant mitigating factor.
CA-CIB has 2027 average core HICP at 2.9%, 30bp above the ECB's 2.6% published in September. The ECB's next forecasts are due 17 December and will be scrutinised.
Market-implied Eurozone inflation recently converged to CA-CIB's forecasts, likely owing to lower energy prices.
